note: FFN replacement only. Every trained arm copies attention, norms, embeddings and the V' head from the b5 D-S checkpoint (ds-ref) and trains 96M more tokens with the b5 recipe. Widths chosen so touched bytes per token match D-S within 1% (check: python budget.py). Arms ds-fresh..kan-bspline form a chain where each differs from the previous in one property; kan-bspline-fit differs from kan-bspline in FFN initialization only.

arms.changes_vs_prev: control for the extra 96M tokens with a trained FFN
control for discarding the trained FFN
gate removed, two matrices, width rescaled to equal bytes
SiLU replaced by learnable safe-Pade rational P5/Q4, shared within 8 channel groups

arms.rational_init: layer 1 identity, layer 2 fit to SiLU (KAT variance-preserving)
arms.changes_vs_prev: rational unit applied to the inputs of both linear maps (KAT GR-KAN layout)

arms.input_norm: existing pre-FFN RMSNorm; inner layer LayerNorm without affine to keep inputs in grid range
arms.changes_vs_prev: per-edge cubic B-spline (G=5) plus SiLU base, efficient-KAN layout

arms.init: ds-ref non-FFN, FFN fitted per layer to ds-ref FFN

fit.objective: per-layer MSE between KAN FFN output and D-S FFN output on D-S hidden states

arms.changes_vs_prev: initialization only: each KAN FFN pre-fitted to the D-S FFN, then the same KD run

stop_if: No KAN arm (gr-kan, kan-bspline, kan-bspline-fit) beats both ds-fresh and mlp-silu on general-prose offline greedy agreement outside the paired bootstrap CI: report negative, do not build the llama.cpp runtime path. kan-bspline-fit is also compared with ds-cont (both start from the trained FFN function).
